title: Precision and output change the query cost
coverage: Three primary sources: the SODA 2026 n^(3/2) estimator, two independent October 2026 n^(4/3) preprints, and the explicit-output quadratic obstruction. Elementary scan baselines are labeled separately.

The pair-query interpretation follows the same search argument: a correct explicit MIS must exclude exactly one endpoint and include every other vertex. This does not lower-bound estimating its size; on that promised family the size is always n−1.

notes: Green denotes algorithms and red lower bounds. Blue and purple distinguish scalar and explicit output.

The two concurrent n^(4/3) preprints share a curve exactly. Triangles identify expected-cost Kiss–Kooroshnezhad; circles identify capped-cost Mahabadi–Tarnawski. Source labels remain separately inspectable.
Historical SODA 2026 n^(3/2) is dashed. No estimation lower bound is supplied or inferred from explicit construction.
With ε=(1/4)n^(-a), the new exponent is 4/3+2a, capped at 2 by scanning. At fixed accuracy the exponent is 4/3; ε=1/4 is an illustrative reference.
The new exponent crossover is a=1/3. Suppressed constants and logarithms can shift a finite-n crossover.

All scalar algorithms choose their own permutation; no claim is made for an externally prescribed MIS or the expectation of its size. Their estimate directions and runtime guarantees remain explicit in theorem details.
